description.narrative:
Project Outcome: Stakeholders Effect Improved access to affordable housing finance, including for women borrowers: IFC anticipates the Project will significantly increase access to housing finance and thus encourage homeownership in the EWS/LIG segments, including for women. Rapid urbanization in India has led to serious development challenges including congestion, pressure on basic amenities, and severe housing shortages in cities, especially, in the low-cost segment. India's mortgage market depth is low compared to emerging economies (India- 10% vs China - 18%, Thailand - 20%). This Project will increase access to housing finance for EWS/LIG segments, with a focus on women borrowers.
Improved access to green affordable housing finance: Limited penetration of green housing is a key challenge in Indian housing market. IFC estimates total green buildings/housing investment opportunity of US$1.4 trillion in India from 2018-2030. The project will support IIFL HF in building its green affordable housing portfolio.
Contribution to Market Creation
Competitiveness: IFCs support to the Project, along with IFCs other systematic engagements in the segment, will promote greater competitiveness in the affordable housing market, including supporting the development of green affordable housing. Housing market in India is very active with banks, NBFCs and HFCs, however, a large portion focuses on higher income groups, and low & middle-income groups remain unserved/underserved.
Although IFC has been supporting the development of affordable housing financiers through continued interventions, the shortage is substantial and would require continuous support. Climate finance deficit in India is large at US$448 billion, and the market for green affordable housing finance remains underdeveloped. Very few HFCs/FIs are focused on financing green buildings/housing, as green finance is perceived to be expensive and thus not considered suitable for the affordable housing segment.

The proposed project is a senior secured loan (or INR bond) of up to US$100 million equivalent to a new client, IIFL Home Finance Limited (IIFL HF or the Company), for a tenor of up to 6 years (the Project). The Project will involve proceeds being used to promote affordable housing for women borrowers from Economically Weaker Sections (EWS) and Low Income Groups (LIG) segments. Discussions are also underway for part of the proceeds to be used for financing retail purchases of green affordable housing. The Company is in the process of discussing an Advisory project to help develop its green affordable housing business. The project is expected to be supported by the Market Accelerator for Green Construction (MAGC) Program as described in the Blended Finance Section.
